**Analysis:**

The image shows a close-up of soybean stems and petioles with the following key features:
- Elongated, brown to reddish-purple lesions/cankers running along the stem and petiole surfaces
- The discoloration is irregular and follows the stem lengthwise
- Green soybean pods visible in background (appearing relatively healthy)
- Some tan/brown fibrous material visible at the node junction
- No fluffy white mycelium, no powdery coating, no angular leaf spots

**Matching against classes:**

- **Anthracnose**: "Brown, irregularly shaped spots on stems, pods and petioles; brown cankers can appear on petioles causing defoliation." The brownish-reddish-purple elongated cankers on stems and petioles match well.
- **White Mold**: Would show fluffy white growth and black sclerotia at nodes — not present here.
- **Brown Stem Rot / SDS**: Primarily internal pith discoloration; the lesions here appear surface/vascular on stems.
- **Fusarium**: Reddish-brown vascular discoloration more internal; possible but less likely without root symptoms visible.

The dominant feature — brown to reddish-purple elongated surface cankers/lesions on petioles and stems of a soybean plant with pods present — aligns most closely with **Anthracnose**.
